Subject: Inference slate: prioritized shortlist & next steps (benchmarks + prompts)

Hi Elena / Jorge — thanks again for the demo today. Great discussion; below is a concise post-demo recap with a recommended inference slate, rationale (cost / latency / quality), links, and concrete next actions so we can keep momentum.

1) Recommended shortlist (prioritized)
- Redwood-Serve-small-8q (recommended pilot): Median token latency ~45ms, p95 ~120ms, estimated cost ~$0.80 / 1k tokens. Tradeoff: excellent throughput and very low cost, reasonable on instruction-following for TempSci taxonomy but weaker on long-context coherent summarization.
- Llama2-13B-q8 + Redwood kernels (balanced): Median token latency ~70ms, p95 ~180ms, estimated cost ~$1.75 / 1k tokens. Tradeoff: stronger quality on multi-step prompts and domain-specific terminology, modestly higher cost.
- OpenBench-70B-8bit (quality-first): Median token latency ~140ms, p95 ~320ms, estimated cost ~$5.20 / 1k tokens. Tradeoff: best quality for corner-case scientific reasoning but higher latency and unit cost.

2) Where these numbers come from
- Benchmarks: we ran the TempSci sample workload (10k query mix) across our dedicated inference profiles — aggregated CSV attached (benchmarks_tempsci_10k_queries.csv) and full results here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1TempsciBenchmarks
- Prompt set: a curated prompt pack for your use cases is attached (tempsci_prompt_pack_v1.zip). It includes canonical instructions, negative examples, and candidate few-shot exemplars we used in the eval.

3) Quality/regression concerns & guardrails
- Risk: switching to smaller quantized variants can create subtle hallucination regressions on rare entity-resolution flows.
- Proposed mitigation: (a) start with a canary rollout on <2% traffic, (b) capture model outputs for the selected prompt set and run our regression eval daily, (c) automatic rollback on quality delta > 4 percentage points on precision@entity recovery.
- We can configure evaluation monitors tied to prompt sets in Redwood Optimize so you get alerts + example counterfactuals.

4) Suggested next steps (short horizon)
- Confirm the canonical test dataset you want in the loop (CSV + label schema) — Elena / Jorge to share by EOD Mon 4/19.
- Schedule a 60-min eng deep-dive (solutions + your infra) to validate p95 latency under realistic concurrency (I suggest Wed 4/21).
- Procurement: procurement@tempsci.ai — please confirm target PO date; we’ll provide SOW + cost breakdown for pilot (see attached sla_risk_summary.pdf).

5) Quick asks from our side
- Please confirm the three use-case priorities (Summarization -> Q&A -> Entity extraction) so we lock prompt order.
- Let us know if the environment requires specific network egress rules or on-prem options.

I’ve attached the prompt pack and the benchmark CSV. If helpful I can also export the evaluation notebooks to your Drive.

Thanks — looking forward to the eng sync.

Best,

Elena — quick answers and concrete next steps below.

1) p95 end-to-end latency (50 concurrent requests)
- Redwood-Serve-small-8q (pilot): observed p95 ~160ms (includes our edge routing + net RTT in us-west). We can reproduce this in the eng deep-dive with your payloads.
- Llama2-13B-q8: p95 ~240ms at same concurrency on a dedicated 1-GPU profile.

2) Pilot cost estimate (3 months, 5M tokens/day peak)
- Redwood-Serve-small-8q: estimated bill ~ $3,600 / month (variable with token mix) — pilot estimate (3 months): $10.8k.
- Llama2-13B-q8: estimated bill ~ $7,875 / month — pilot estimate (3 months): $23.6k.
- Notes: these include our reserved pilot discount and assume no persistent KV cache charges. Exact numbers change with average response length; we’ll provide per-call cost calc for Procurement.

3) How we instrument precision/quality monitoring
- We’ll wire up a daily regression job: run the canonical prompt pack against candidate model and baseline; compute precision/recall on labeled set; send anomalies to Slack + Redwood Console alerting.
- Canary rollout plan: 0.5% → 2% → 10% traffic ramps with checks at each step. Automatic rollback if precision drops >4 pts or if mean latency increases >30% over baseline.

4) Proposed schedule
- Share canonical dataset by EOD Mon 4/19 (TempSci)
- Eng deep-dive Wed 4/21 10:00–11:00 PT (we’ll send calendar + Zoom)
- Procurement draft SOW by Fri 4/23 (Redwood)

I’ve uploaded the detailed benchmark CSV and a short breakdown to Drive (link below). I’ll also add a short one-page cost breakout for Procurement.
